purpose: Production north-south low bulkhead and limestone end jamb; same geometry and privacy as gate authority.
prompt_text: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: original raster game sprite atlas for Relic Tide. Input image 1 is STYLE REFERENCE ONLY: use its pixel-painted blue limestone, restrained oxidized brass and warm golden edge highlights. Make TWO isolated sprites on a genuinely transparent background, no glow, no ground rectangle, no text. Left two thirds of square atlas: a VERY LONG NARROW NORTH-SOUTH sluice bulkhead segment as seen from overhead in a 2D top-down adventure, similar camera to Eastward. Its total silhouette is about 110 pixels wide and 740 pixels long. It is a LOW wall aligned vertically along screen Y, not a tall upright portrait door: top visible cap of dark brass/wood and a narrow east-facing blue stone/bronze edge, small brass cross straps. Both ends are plain and square to join jambs. Orthographic overhead plan view with modest south-side wall elevation; no isometric slant, no standing panel, no window, no giant circular emblem. Right third of atlas: one squat BLUE LIMESTONE END JAMB, about 170 wide and 150 tall, same overhead perspective, stone blocks with a thin recessed brass guide rail. The jamb is separate, can be reused at both ends. Clear generous alpha gutters, artwork never touching. Uniform sprite palette and crisp painted pixel clusters, small readable material details suitable for reducing the long strip to 24x144 game units and jamb to 30x26. Keep the long strip slender and attached-looking, not a front-facing cabinet. Only these two objects. Transparent alpha outside both sprites.
